text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Reed Elsevier buys U.S. trade journal publisher Chilton Business Group.(p.1)
- Temp employment agency Goudsmit tales over larger sector rival Unique (p.1)
- Dutch emissions of greenhouse gases climbing again after initial reduction. (p.1)
- Central Netherlands paralysed in six-hour power cut. (p.1)
- Engineering consultancy Fugro boosts turnover, profits in first half of 1997. (p.5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Brisk trade in livestock permits as Dutch pig farmers seek to circumvent new restrictions to curb spread of swine fever (p.1)
- Radioactive cargo of medical equipment carried by Dutch airline KLM on London-bound flight last May "not extremely harmful" according to health inspectorate (p.3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Social affairs and employment minister Ad Melkert says government to use next year's tax windfall to boost state pensioners' buying power. (p.1)
- Dutch Royal family taking cruise through Norway (p.1)
- Number of abortions rises in Netherlands in first six months of 1996, possibly due to concerns over health risks associated with so-called 'third generation" contraceptive pills. (p.7)
- Dutch transport sector and petrol stations situated on Dutch-German border to receive compensation when government hikes excise duties on fuel next week. (p.6)
- President Fezi Khalegi Yazdi of Nasdaq-listed automation firm Triple P to step down in September (p.25)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Environment minister Margreet de Boer seeks to cut maximum speed limit on Dutch roads by 10-20 kilometres to fight carbon dioxide emissions (p.5)
TROUW
- Justice minister Winnie Sorgdrager endorses police crackdown on demonstrators in Amsterdam during European summit (p.4)
- Police uncover large-scale fraud in seed potatoes (p.7)
